subject.title: [Bug 6.1] Silent config auto-patch from memory-core + error-message auto-fix breaks all cron jobs on hosts without Docker

question: Should OpenClaw allow agent/plugin/cron-originated config mutations through the CLI/exec path, or should protected config writes require an explicit operator-approved channel with provenance?
rationale: The source still exposes CLI config patching separately from the guarded gateway tool path, and the reported behavior crosses persisted config, exec authority, sandbox posture, and plugin cron provenance; automation cannot choose that trust boundary safely.

options.title: Require explicit operator approval for protected writes
options.body: Keep operator-only repair advice, remove assistant-visible config-write hints, and require provenance or approval for protected config mutations regardless of whether they arrive through gateway tools, CLI-through-exec, or plugin cron work.

options.title: Treat CLI-through-exec as trusted host authority
options.body: Document that agents/plugins with host exec can mutate config through the CLI and limit the fix to clearer audit/provenance warnings around automated cron/plugin writes.

options.title: Limit this to message hardening
options.body: Only remove model-visible sandbox config hints and keep broader CLI/plugin config mutation behavior unchanged for now.

recommendation.title: Require explicit operator approval for protected writes
recommendation.body: Keep operator-only repair advice, remove assistant-visible config-write hints, and require provenance or approval for protected config mutations regardless of whether they arrive through gateway tools, CLI-through-exec, or plugin cron work.

likelyOwner.reason: The central unresolved choice is the config mutation trust boundary, and prior merged work by this person introduced the protected gateway config-write guard.
